ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A metal rod ab of length $10\mathrm{cm}$ is horizontally suspended in a uniform magnetic field by two identical springs; the magnetic induction strength of the field is $0.1\mathrm{T}$, directed perpendicularly into the plane of the paper; the upper ends of the springs are fixed, and the lower ends are insulated from the metal rod. The metal rod is connected through a switch to a battery with an electromotive force of $12\mathrm{V}$, and the total resistance of the circuit is $2\Omega$. It is known that when the switch is open, the elongation of each spring is $0.5\mathrm{cm}$; after closing the switch and the system reaching equilibrium again, the elongation of each spring changes by $0.3\ \mathrm{cm}$ compared to when the switch is open. The gravitational acceleration is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. Determine the direction of the Ampere force acting on the metal rod after the switch is closed.
2. What is the mass of the metal rod?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
The direction is vertically downward.
0.01 kg

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a metal rod is placed horizontally, with the left end labeled a and the right end labeled b; the rod is suspended under the upper fixed support by two identical vertical springs on the left and right. In the magnetic-field region, multiple “×” are drawn, indicating that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward, and B is also labeled in the figure. Below the metal rod, a battery and a switch are connected through wires. After the switch is closed, according to the battery connection direction in the figure, the direction of the conventional current through the metal rod is from b to a, that is, leftward along the rod. Reasoning: The current direction is leftward, and the magnetic-field direction is perpendicular to the paper surface inward. Using the direction rule for Ampere force or the vector relation F = I L × B, the leftward current interacts with the inward magnetic field, and the direction of the Ampere force on the metal rod is vertically downward. The circuit current is I = E/R = 12/2 = 6 A. The length of the metal rod L = 10 cm = 0.10 m, so the magnitude of the Ampere force F_A = BIL = 0.1 × 6 × 0.10 = 0.06 N. When the switch is open, the two identical springs jointly support the metal rod, and there is 2kx_0 = mg, where x_0 = 0.5 cm = 0.005 m. After the switch is closed, the Ampere force is downward, causing each spring to extend additionally by Δx = 0.3 cm = 0.003 m, so the newly added spring force satisfies 2kΔx = F_A. Dividing the two equations gives mg/F_A = x_0/Δx, so m = F_A x_0/(g Δx) = 0.06 × 0.005/(10 × 0.003) = 0.01 kg.
